He played [[college basketball]] for [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State University]], and was drafted 38th overall by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. Weaver, a {{convert|6|ft|6|in|m|adj=on}} [[shooting guard]]-[[small forward]], was born in [[Beloit, Wisconsin]]. His father, [[LaMont Weaver]], played collegiate basketball at the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison|University of Wisconsin]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/preps/40453927.html|title=Weaver's heave in 1969 remains clear to all 40 years later}}[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/lamont-weaver-1.html LaMont Weaver]. sportsreference.com ==High school== Weaver attended [[Beloit Memorial High School]], in [[Beloit, Wisconsin|Beloit]], [[Wisconsin]], where he played high school basketball.{{Cite web|title=Kyle Weaver Profile - The Washington State University Official Athletic Site|url=https://wsucougars.com/news/2013/4/18/208185823.aspx|access-date=2021-01-11|website=Washington State University Athletics|date=18 April 2013 |language=en}} ==College career== Weaver had a career-high 25 points and 12 rebounds in a 75–68 [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]] loss to [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] on March 14, 2008, at the [[Staples Center]], in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/280740024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230702042646/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/280740024|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 2, 2023|title=Washington State 68-75 Stanford (Mar 14, 2008) Game Recap|website=ESPN}} ==Professional career== On August 11, 2008, Weaver was traded by the Charlotte Bobcats to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], for a second-round draft pick from the [[2009 NBA draft]], which originally belonged to the [[New Jersey Nets]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/weaver_trade_080811.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090307173918/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/weaver_trade_080811.html|url-status=dead|title=Bobcats Acquire 2009 Second-Round Draft Pick|website=[[NBA.com]] |archivedate=March 7, 2009}} The Thunder assigned Weaver to the [[NBA Development League]] affiliate [[Tulsa 66ers]], in April 2009,[http://www.nba.com/dleague/tulsa/weaver_090401.html Oklahoma City’s Weaver Assigned To Tulsa 66ers]. April 1, 2009. November 2009,[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/thunder_091121.html Oklahoma City Assigns Kyle Weaver and Byron Mullens To Tulsa]. November 21, 2009. March 2010,[http://www.nba.com/dleague/tulsa/thunder_100302.html Thunder Assigned Mullens and Weaver To Tulsa]. March 2, 2010. and April 2010.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/tulsa/weaver_100408.html Thunder Assign Kyle Weaver To Tulsa]. April 8, 2010. Weaver spent the 2010 training camp with the [[Chicago Bulls]],K.C. Johnson. "Heat don't intimidate Bulls". ''Chicago Tribune''. September 28, 2010. but he was waived on October 21. After spending several months in the NBA D-League, he was signed by the [[Utah Jazz]], on March 30, 2011.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/kyle_weaver_signs_with_utah_2011_03_30.html|title=Austin's Kyle Weaver Signs With Utah|website=[[NBA.com]] }} In April 2011, he signed with [[Spirou Charleroi]] in Belgium.{{Cite web |url=http://newsdesk.thebasketballpost.com/2011/04/20/spirou-basket-signs-kyle-weaver.aspx |title=Spirou Basket Signs Kyle Weaver |access-date=April 21, 2011 |archive-date=April 26, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110426082216/http://newsdesk.thebasketballpost.com/2011/04/20/spirou-basket-signs-kyle-weaver.aspx |url-status=usurped }} In July 2011, he joined the German team [[Alba Berlin]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/euroleague/news/|title=Latest News | EuroLeague|date=October 19, 2023|website=Euroleague Basketball}}{{Dead link|date=January 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} In October 2012, he signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/2012/10/grizzlies-add-ronald-murray-and-kyle-weaver-to-training-camp/|title=Grizzlies add Ronald Murray and Kyle Weaver to training camp – NBA Blog – NBA Basketball Blog|date=October 1, 2012}} On October 23, 2012, Weaver was waived by the Grizzlies. Weaver then signed with the [[Austin Toros]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/austin_toros_announce_returning_players_2012_11_01.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004221216/http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/austin_toros_announce_returning_players_2012_11_01.html|url-status=dead|title=Austin Toros Announce 2012-13 Returning Players and Camp Invitees|website=[[NBA.com]] |archivedate=October 4, 2013}} On February 25, 2013, Weaver was traded to the [[Canton Charge]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/farrakhan_johnson_added_2013_02_25.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307082739/http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/farrakhan_johnson_added_2013_02_25.html|url-status=dead|title=IDAHO ACQUIRES FARRAKHAN, JOHNSON|website=[[NBA.com]] |archivedate=March 7, 2013}} On August 19, 2013, he signed a one-year deal with [[Azzurro Napoli Basket 2013|Azzurro Napoli]].{{cite web|title=Azzurro Napoli Basket lands Kyle Weaver|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/legadue/61771/azzurro-napoli-basket-lands-kyle-weaver.html|publisher=Sportando.net|access-date=19 August 2013}} On October 28, 2014, he signed with [[Bnei Herzliya]] of Israel, for the 2014–15 season.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/139173/kyle-weaver-signs-in-israel-with-bnei-herzliya.html|title=Kyle Weaver signs in Israel with Bnei Herzliya}} On January 9, 2015, he was released by the Israeli team.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/147943/bnei-herzliya-signs-julian-wright-and-deron-washington.html|title=Bnei Herzliya signs Julian Wright and Deron Washington}} On March 7, he signed with [[Caciques de Humacao]], of the Puerto Rican [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/154657/caciques-de-humacao-sign-dan-jennings-and-kyle-weaver.html|title=Caciques de Humacao sign Dan Jennings and Kyle Weaver}} He left the club after appearing in only two games.
